title: Scan indexing, retrieval, graph, storage, and context-pack surfaces for missed shared-module adoption
scope: H31 core product-surface scan across src/index/**, src/retrieval/**, src/graph/**, src/storage/**, src/context-pack/**, and src/map/**.

summary.overallAssessment: This part of the codebase already makes heavy use of shared modules, especially artifact IO, truncation, limits, sort, provenance, and runtime-envelope helpers. The right outcome here is selective consolidation, not broad flattening. The strongest missed adoption cases are context-pack assembly still managing raw truncation arrays instead of consistently using the shared truncation recorder, repeated local path-normalization wrappers that should collapse onto existing shared path/files helpers, and a problematic cluster of product surfaces still reaching into tools/shared/dict-utils.js where that dependency should not spread further.

highestPriorityHotspots.whyItMatters: Context-pack assembly is one of the main evidence surfaces, and raw truncation-array handling is easier to drift or under-report than the shared truncation recorder already used by graph and retrieval flows.
Indexing, map, graph, and storage surfaces still define small local toPosix/path-normalization helpers, which invites subtle casing and relative-path drift.

highestPriorityHotspots.category: product code depending on tool-side dict-utils
highestPriorityHotspots.whyItMatters: This is a cross-layer dependency seam that should be reduced, not expanded, because it couples core product code to tool-oriented config/cache helpers.
highestPriorityHotspots.bestCurrentHandling: Treat as a no-adopt / follow-up extraction candidate rather than broadening tools/shared usage.

hotspotMatrix.name: Context-pack assembly uses raw truncation arrays instead of the shared recorder
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Standardize context-pack truncation collection on the shared truncation recorder and keep raw arrays only at the final surface-shaping boundary if needed for schema compatibility.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: Graph and retrieval surfaces already use the recorder successfully. Reusing it here reduces evidence-completeness drift without inventing another truncation contract.
testsToRequire: context-pack strict-evidence and parity tests whenever truncation collection changes
context-pack output contract tests where truncation payload shape matters

hotspotMatrix.name: Repeated path-normalization wrappers around existing shared helpers
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Collapse trivial toPosix/path wrappers onto the shared files/path-normalize helpers and leave only domain-specific naming or validation wrappers in place.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: Most of these wrappers are not policy-bearing; they are convenience layers over the same canonical normalization behavior.
testsToRequire: path/canonicalization regressions where case-insensitive or escaped-path handling matters
storage/index/map tests that depend on repo-relative path formatting

hotspotMatrix.name: Core product surfaces still depend on tools/shared/dict-utils.js
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Do not spread this dependency further. Use this scan result to drive extraction of proper src-shared repo/cache/runtime helpers in later H32 work instead of adopting tools/shared more deeply.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: H30 already showed that dict-utils is the wrong long-term ownership seam. Expanding it would increase the cleanup cost.
testsToRequire: no immediate migration under #417 unless a replacement shared surface exists
follow-on extraction should preserve current cache-root/build-pointer/runtime behavior through targeted regression tests

hotspotMatrix.name: Graph/context/retrieval surfaces already align well on truncation and provenance
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Keep the current shared adoption pattern and avoid over-consolidating the domain-specific traversal logic itself.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: These surfaces already share the right primitives while preserving domain-specific semantics. Further hoisting here would risk flattening useful distinctions.

hotspotMatrix.name: Artifact IO adoption is strong; avoid replacing local domain transforms with generic shared IO
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Treat this as a no-adopt zone beyond small helper cleanups. The shared IO layer is already doing its job; keep domain-specific transformation logic local.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: These modules already consume the canonical IO surfaces. Forcing more logic into shared IO would mix domain transforms with low-level storage concerns.

mappings.problemSurface: Context-pack truncation collection and evidence shaping
Product code pulling runtime/cache helpers from tool-side dict-utils
mappings.noAdoptRationale: Do not deepen tools/shared/dict-utils adoption here; this seam should be addressed by H32 extraction work instead.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainLocal: Already uses shared limits, truncation, and sort helpers correctly; the traversal semantics themselves are domain-specific.
Already aligned on shared primitives; additional hoisting would mostly flatten graph-domain behavior.
Same rationale as graph impact and neighborhood: shared primitives are already in place.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainMostlyLocal: SQLite build planning, execution, and ingestion are storage-domain specific even when they correctly depend on shared IO and normalization helpers.
Retrieval staging, ranking, and fusion logic should remain local; only the generic helpers around limits, truncation, normalization, and serialization should be shared.
Client rendering helpers are presentation-domain specific; only low-level iterables/path normalization should be shared.

recommendedFollowUps.why: The tooling/setup/bench scan should handle related path/env/helper seams that sit outside the core product tree.
The dict-utils cross-layer seam should turn into a real repo/workspace/cache-root/generation helper family instead of spreading further.
If context-pack/risk/search normalization still feels fragmented after H31 adoption, formalize a shared search/risk/context-pack helper family.
If path/serialization cleanup reveals more low-level duplication, capture it in the filesystem/JSON/persistence helper issue.
